# How it works

gx adds a context layer around your existing Git workflow. It captures what
happened during coding sessions, attaches that context to ordinary Git commits,
and uses it for two review surfaces: `gx review` locally and generated PR
summaries on GitHub.

## The problem

Git was built for humans typing commits one at a time. A commit stores a
snapshot and a short message, and for human-paced work that is usually enough.

Agent-written code breaks two of Git's assumptions:

1. **The context that explains a change never makes it into the repo.** The
   prompt that asked for the change, the commands the agent ran, the tests it
   executed, the dead ends it backed out of — all of that lives in a session
   transcript that is gone by review time. The commit message is whatever one
   line survived.
2. **Review is now the bottleneck.** The cost of generating code is dropping
   toward zero, but teams still review line by line. When a pull request is one
   large undifferentiated diff with a thin message, the reviewer reconstructs
   intent from scratch.

## What gx captures

- **Sessions** — transcripts from Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. The pre-push
  hook captures them into `~/.gx/gx.db` and publishes them alongside
  the code they produced.
- **Revisions** — each plain `git commit` is recorded as one reviewable unit,
  down to individual hunks. gx links each revision to the session that
  produced it by matching the changed hunks against captured session activity —
  nothing is attached by hand.

## How gx review works

`gx review` reads the current change — a dirty working tree, or the branch's
commits against its base — and reviews it with two independent AI reviewers
plus repo context: the indexed codebase, captured sessions, review history, and
your repo's review policy. A judge model then verifies and dedupes the
findings. Alongside them it runs what the project already has — the compiler,
the linter, the test suite, a secret scan over added lines, and the dependency
audits when a manifest moved — and reports those results as evidence rather
than as a separate command.

Findings land in two lanes, and the split is what makes the verdict worth
trusting. A finding is **blocking** only when both reviewers raised it
independently *and* the verification model confirmed it; anything one model
raised alone is **advisory** — reported, but it will not stop you. Agreement
between independent readers is the strongest confidence signal a panel
produces, so gx spends it on the only decision that matters: ship or don't.

The run ends in that verdict — `SHIP`, `NO-SHIP`, `DEGRADED` when the panel
could not fully run, or `NOTHING-TO-REVIEW`. Because a pass is a claim about
code that was actually inspected, the last two cases are failures rather than
quiet zeros.

The command touches no Git state — no hooks, no commits, no index mutation, and
no `~/.gx` on a machine that never ran `gx init` — so it runs anywhere,
including CI (the exit code gates by default) and checkouts you do not own. The
one file it writes is the report itself, saved to `review/` and added to your
local Git excludes so it never shows up as a change. See the
[CLI reference](/docs/cli#gx-review).

## How PR summaries work

On `git push`, the pre-push hook uploads a review bundle: the revisions, their
hunks, and the linked sessions. When a pull request exists, gx Cloud
generates a summary from that bundle plus the indexed codebase, and writes it
into the PR description below your own text.

The summary opens with a verdict — 🟢 **Quick scan**, 🟡 **Careful pass**, or
🔴 **Deep review** — judged by blast radius: what the change can break,
including code the diff never touches. Notable Changes each carry an
`Attribution:` line naming the concrete source that informed them. See
[Pull Requests](/docs/pull-requests).

## Why this speeds up review

- The verdict tells a reviewer how much attention a PR needs before they open
  the diff. A two-file rename that breaks downstream consumers gets 🔴; a
  contained refactor gets 🟢.
- Notable Changes point at the hunks that decide correctness, so the mechanical
  rest can be skimmed instead of read line by line.
- Session provenance answers "why is this here?" without a round-trip to the
  author — the prompt, commands, and tests are part of the review context.
- `gx review` catches findings before the PR exists, when they are cheapest to
  fix.

## Everything is still just Git

The hooks publish normal Git branches and commits; sessions and metadata go to
gx Cloud as a review bundle. Nothing about your repository becomes
gx-specific — if you stop using gx tomorrow, your branches and
commits remain ordinary Git.

---

# Getting Started

gx records which agent session produced each Git commit and uses that context
for AI code review and generated pull request summaries. You work in plain Git.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth login
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # or OPENAI_API_KEY
```

This installs bash/zsh completions and the `gxr` shorthand for `gx review`.
Review runs a model on your machine, so it needs an API key; the hooks, capture,
and PR summaries do not.

## Basic Usage

The everyday flow is two gx commands: `gx init` once per repository to install
the Git hooks, and `gx review` before you ship. Otherwise, use Git as normal —
the hooks record revisions, capture sessions, and publish on push without any
gx-specific commands.

```bash
cd your-repo
gx init                                # once per repo: installs the Git hooks
git add src/retry.js
git commit -m "add retry helper"       # hook records the revision
gx review                              # AI review and ship / no-ship verdict
git push                               # hook captures the session and publishes
gh pr create                           # gx Cloud adds the summary to the PR
```

Summaries require the [gx GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx)
on the account or org that owns the repo.

## Uninstall

```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/gx ~/.local/bin/gxr ~/.local/bin/gx-mcp
rm -f ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/gx ~/.zfunc/_gx
```

Installed Git hooks exit silently when the binary is absent, so plain Git keeps
working. Local data remains in `~/.gx`.

## Pages

- [CLI](/docs/cli) — every command: `gx init`, `gx review`, `gx enhance`, `gx auth`, `gx doctor`
- [MCP](/docs/mcp) — connect `gx_review` to Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
- [Pull Requests](/docs/pull-requests) — generated PR summaries and `@gx` chat on GitHub

---

# CLI

Initialize any repository with `gx init`. This installs git hooks that capture
your session context and pairs it with your code changes, giving gx
better context for review.

## gx CLI Overview

```bash
gx init         # set up hooks in a repo (run once)
gx review       # AI review and pre-ship verdict for the current change (alias: gxr)
gx enhance      # the single highest-value fix, written for your coding model
gx auth         # sign in to gx Cloud
gx doctor       # diagnose capture, hooks, and publishing
gx version      # print the version
```

`gx review` and `gx enhance` call a model, so they need an API key:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # or OPENAI_API_KEY
```

## gx init

```bash
gx init
```

`gx init` installs the Git hooks and registers the MCP server. Run it once per
repository.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | user name to store in gx config (defaults to Git identity) |
| `--email <email>` | user email to store in gx config |
| `-y`, `--yes` | accept defaults and suppress prompts — use in scripts and agent sandboxes |
| `--global` | install the hooks machine-wide instead of for one repository |

### Global hooks

```bash
gx init --global
```

Installs the hooks once for every repository. The scripts chain to each
repository's own hooks of the same name, so husky, lefthook, and hand-written
hooks keep working. If a global hooks path is already set to something else,
`gx init --global` stops rather than overwriting it.

Opt a single repository out, from inside it:

```bash
git config gx.enabled false
```

Undo the machine-wide install:

```bash
git config --global --unset core.hooksPath
```

## gx review

```bash
gx review                                     # alias: gxr
gx review "make checkout survive gateway blips"
gx review --scope security                    # focused pass
gx review --focus src/auth --deep             # deep review of one directory
gx review --base origin/main --md             # markdown report, e.g. for a PR comment
```

Reviews the current change and ends in a ship / no-ship verdict. Two
independent reviewers read the change against your indexed codebase, captured
sessions, review history, and your repo's review policy; a verification model
then confirms and dedupes what they found. This can be run in the terminal or
via [MCP](/docs/mcp).

### Intent

The optional positional argument is one sentence saying what the change was
meant to do, in your words — `"fix the auth timeout"`. It is not a question and
not a filter. The reviewer holds the diff against it, so a change that quietly
does more than the intent says is itself a finding. With no intent, gx derives
one from the branch name and recent commit subjects, and says so in the report.

### Lanes

Every finding lands in one of two lanes:

| Lane | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BLOCKING` | stops the change — this is what exits non-zero |
| `ADVISORY` | reported, and does not fail the gate |

A finding blocks only when **both** reviewers raised it and the verification
model confirmed it. One model's opinion — however strongly worded — is demoted
to advisory.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[intent]` | optional positional sentence stating what the change is meant to do |
| `--base <ref>` | review the commit range `<ref>...HEAD` instead of the working tree |
| `--scope <name>` | focused lens: `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `--focus <path>` | limit the review to files under a path prefix |
| `--repo` | review the whole repository rather than the current change; wins over `--base` |
| `--deep` | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `--fast` | optimize for wall clock: one reviewer, no verification pass, no code examples in findings |
| `--verbose` | include repo facts, docs, and changed files |
| `--json` | print the report as JSON |
| `--md` | print the report as markdown — the PR-comment body |
| `--max-findings <n>` | cap how many recommendations the review reports |
| `--fail-on <level>` | exit non-zero when findings at or above this level survive (default `blocking`) |
| `--no-comment` | skip posting the PR review comment, but still record review history |
| `--no-publish` | skip both the PR review comment and the review history |
| `--client <name>` | label the surface invoking this review: `cli`, `mcp`, `skill`, `slash-gx` |

### What gets reviewed

1. `--repo` when given — the whole repository
2. `--base <ref>` when given — the range `<ref>...HEAD`
3. Otherwise a dirty working tree
4. Otherwise the branch's commits against an auto-detected base (`main`,
   `master`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`), or the last commit when HEAD is
   the base branch

If nothing was found, `gx review` says so. "Nothing was reviewed" is its own
outcome and never counts as a clean pass.

### Checks that are not the model

Alongside the reviewers, `gx review` runs whatever the project already has, and
reports the results as evidence:

| Check | When it runs |
| --- | --- |
| `go test`, `go vet`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest`, `cargo check`, `dart analyze`, `flutter analyze`, `dotnet build` | when the change touches that ecosystem |
| secret scan over added lines (`security.secret-in-added-lines`) | every review — added lines only, since a removed secret is the fix, not the leak |
| dependency audits: `govulncheck`, `npm audit`, `pip-audit` | when the change touches a manifest or lockfile, or under `--repo` |

A missing tool is never a failure — an auditor that isn't installed is reported
as skipped evidence. Set `GX_REVIEW_STATIC_TOOLS=0` to turn the whole set off.

### The report

Under a terminal the report opens as an accordion you walk section by section:
the two lanes, a **FIX PLAN**, and the story of the change. Piped or in CI it
prints in full instead, and the exit code is the same either way.

The last two lines are the machine seam — `Verdict:` and `Next:`:

| Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `SHIP` | no blocking finding |
| `NO-SHIP` | at least one blocking finding survived |
| `DEGRADED` | no blocking finding, but the panel did not fully run — a pass would be unearned |
| `NOTHING-TO-REVIEW` | no change was found |

Every run that inspected code also saves its full JSON report to
`review/review-findings-<timestamp>.json`, and adds `/review/` to
`.git/info/exclude` so the saved reports never dirty `git status`.

### As a CI gate

The gate is on by default — no opt-in flag needed:

```bash
gx review --base origin/main --no-publish
```

`--fail-on` sets the threshold:

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blocking` | **default** — only findings in the blocking lane (both reviewers plus the verifier) |
| `strong` | findings at `strong` strength or above, whatever the lane |
| `worth-exploring` | findings at `worth-exploring` strength or above |
| `speculative` | findings at `speculative` strength or above |
| `any` | anything the review raised |
| `none` | turn the gate off |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | reviewed, and nothing at or above the threshold survived |
| `3` | findings at or above the threshold survived |
| `4` | nothing was reviewed — a gate should not pass without inspecting code |
| `5` | degraded — the review ran incomplete, so a pass would be unearned |

Pair with `--no-publish` so CI never posts PR comments, and `--json` to parse
findings yourself.

### Swapping the model panel

`GX_REVIEW_MODELS=<preset>` swaps reviewers and judge together:

```bash
GX_REVIEW_MODELS=budget gx review
```

| Preset | Panel |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Haiku + Sonnet 4.6 reviewing, Haiku judging |
| `budget` | Haiku + GLM 5 reviewing, Nemotron 3 Super judging |
| `luna` | GPT-5.6 Luna end to end |
| `glm` | GLM 5 end to end |

A single slot's own environment variable still wins over the preset.

### Read-only

`gx review` changes no Git state — no commits, no index mutation, no hooks, and
no `~/.gx` on a machine that never ran `gx init` (which is required for PR
summaries and chat, not for review). The saved report above is the only file it
writes, and it is excluded from Git.

## gx enhance

```bash
gx enhance                            # alias: gx gxe
gx enhance "fix the auth timeout"
gx enhance | pbcopy
gx enhance | claude -p "apply this"
```

Prints the single change most worth making right now, written as a prompt you
hand to a coding model: the problem, the code it lives in, the change to make,
and how to know it worked.

It runs the same review as `gx review` and reports the top of that review's fix
plan — blocking findings first, then the judge's ranking — so the two never
disagree about what matters most. `gx enhance` is `gx review`'s answer, narrowed
to one item and rewritten for a model rather than a person.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[intent]` | optional positional sentence stating what the change is meant to do |
| `--base <ref>` | review the commit range `<ref>...HEAD` instead of the working tree |
| `--focus <path>` | limit the review to files under a path prefix |
| `--repo` | review the whole repository rather than the current change |
| `--deep` | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `--fast` | optimize for wall clock: one reviewer, no verification pass |

Output is plain text on stdout, so it pipes. Exit status is always `0` — gating
is `gx review`'s job. When the review finds nothing to fix, `gx enhance` says so
on stderr and stdout stays empty.

## gx auth

```bash
gx auth login
gx auth status
gx auth logout
```

Signs the CLI into gx Cloud through GitHub.

## gx doctor

```bash
gx doctor            # diagnose capture, hooks, auth, and the publish queue
gx doctor --fix      # apply safe repairs
gx doctor --json     # machine-readable report
gx doctor --report   # send this diagnosis and recent logs to support
```

## gx version

```bash
gx version
gx version --json
```

## Shortcuts

The installer links `gxr` to the same binary, so a review is one word:

```bash
gxr   # gx review
```

`gx gxr` and `gx gxe` work as subcommand aliases for `gx review` and
`gx enhance`.

---

# MCP

The MCP server ships with the CLI as a local stdio binary. It shells out to the
CLI, so repo state stays on your machine. It exposes one tool: `gx_review`.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth login
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # or OPENAI_API_KEY — the review calls a model
```

## Register with your agent

`gx init` registers the server automatically with agent CLIs found on your
`PATH` (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and reports something like
`MCP ok: Claude Code, Cursor`.

To register with every MCP client on your machine in one command, use
[`add-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/add-mcp):

```bash
npx add-mcp @satoricorp/gx --name gx -g -y
```

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-g` | install user-level so gx is available in every project; omit for project-level config |
| `-y` | non-interactive (skip prompts) |
| `-a <agent>` | target a specific agent (repeatable), e.g. `-a cursor` |

Most clients load MCP servers at startup — restart the client or open a new
chat after registering.

For clients neither path covers, the stdio shape is:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gx": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@satoricorp/gx"]
    }
  }
}
```

The server finds the CLI in `~/.local/bin` or on `PATH`; set `GX_BINARY`
to point somewhere else.

## gx_review

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | optional intent, e.g. `"fix the auth timeout"` — passed as the positional argument, and the reviewer holds the diff against it |
| `scope` | enum | focused lens: `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `focus` | string | limit review to files under this path prefix |
| `deep` | boolean | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `fast` | boolean | optimize for wall clock: one reviewer, no verification pass — for reviews someone is waiting on |
| `verbose` | boolean | include repo facts, docs, and changed files |
| `repo` | boolean | review the whole repository instead of the current change |
| `cwd` | string | repository working directory (defaults to the MCP server process cwd) |

Runs `gx review --no-comment --client mcp`, so an agent asking for review
context never comments on a pull request — commenting stays a deliberate act of
the CLI, where a human typed the command. The run itself still records to gx
Cloud history, so MCP reviews count in per-surface usage; use the `gx review
--no-publish` CLI flag to suppress that too.

The tool is read-only and never initializes a repository. May run up to 5
minutes. A no-ship verdict is a successful tool call, not an error — the verdict
lives in the report's final `Verdict:` / `Next:` lines, with the blocking and
advisory lanes and a **FIX PLAN** above them. See
[the CLI reference](/docs/cli#gx-review) for what those mean.

Saving and publishing are plain Git, not MCP calls: `git add` + `git commit`
record the revision through the hooks, `git push` captures and publishes.

## AGENTS.md instructions

`gx init` offers to append these instructions to your repo's `AGENTS.md`. If you
skipped that step, add them manually:

```markdown
# Agents

Version control: plain Git. Once `gx init` installs the hooks, gx records and publishes automatically — there is no gx save verb.

Default flow:
- Run `git add` to stage the files for this revision.
- Run `git commit -m "..."` to save. A gx hook records the commit as a reviewable revision.
- Run plain `git push` to publish. The gx pre-push hook captures the session and publishes code changes, sessions, and gx metadata to gx Cloud automatically — do not run `gx push` or `gx capture push` yourself; they bypass the hook.
- Open PRs with `gh pr create` (or the GitHub UI). Do not seed a `## Summary` in the PR body — leave human notes only; gx Cloud appends the rich summary below once the PR exists.
- To amend, use `git commit --amend` and preserve the gx revision trailer in the message.

For AI review, run the `gx_review` MCP tool (or the `gx review` CLI) on the current change.
```

---

# Pull Requests

gx writes a review summary into your pull request description and answers
questions when you mention `@gx` in PR comments. See [Getting Started](/docs)
for instructions.

## PR summaries

gx appends a summary to your pull request description, with links and
attribution for the important changes.

Section Descriptions:

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict line | 🟢 **Quick scan** (LOW) / 🟡 **Careful pass** (MEDIUM) / 🔴 **Deep review** (HIGH), plus a one-line triage reason. The label always matches the Blast Radius level |
| Overview | What changed and why |
| Blast Radius | severity with file/area/line counts and a risk note. Judged by what the change can break — including code the diff never touches — not by diff size |
| Notable Changes | the changes a reviewer should look at first, each with an `Attribution:` line naming the concrete source: a codebase path, a captured agent session, a prior PR, or docs |

Summaries are generated when the GitHub App sees `pull_request`
`opened`/`synchronize` for a branch with published gx context, and after a
publish when a PR already exists. Push again to force a refresh.

## Chat with @gx

Mention `@gx` in any PR comment:

```text
@gx which files should I review first?
@gx explain the auth callback changes
@gx what is the highest-risk change in this PR?
@gx are there missing tests?
```

Any answer from `@gx` will cite its source (codebase, previous PRs, past
sessions, etc). `@gx` can answer questions based on outcomes from sessions,
giving your team full transparency into every coding session.

### Retire a learned rule

```text
@gx skip rule never use var
@gx do not enforce this migration naming rule
```

When a matching active rule exists, it is retired and the override recorded.
Requires **write**, **maintain**, or **admin** permission on the repository.

---

# gx changelog: new features, updates, and fixes

## August 16, 2026

**`gx review` is the pre-ship verdict** — Two commands that both ended in a ship /
no-ship verdict was one too many, so `gx gates` (briefly `gx constraints`) is gone
and `gx review` is the single gate. The deterministic checks the gate owned moved
into review rather than disappearing with it: the secret scan over added lines, the
dependency audits (`govulncheck`, `npm audit`, `pip-audit`) when a manifest or
lockfile moved, and `pytest` on Python projects — all three now run on the command
that hooks and CI actually call. The `gxc`/`gxg` shorthands and the `gx_constraints`
MCP tool retire with it; `gxr` is the shorthand, `gx_review` the tool.

**Blocking and advisory lanes** — Findings now split by how much agreement is behind
them. A finding blocks only when both reviewers raised it independently *and* the
verification model confirmed it; one model's opinion is advisory and will not stop
you. `--fail-on blocking` is the default, so the exit code gates without an opt-in
flag, and `--fail-on none` turns it off.

**Intent, not a prompt** — The positional argument is now one sentence saying what the
change was meant to do — `gx review "fix the auth timeout"` — rather than a question or a
filter. The reviewer holds the diff against it, so a change that quietly does more than
its stated intent is itself a finding. Omit it and gx derives one from the branch name
and recent commit subjects, and says so in the report.

**`gx enhance`** — Prints the single highest-value fix in the current change as a
prompt written for a coding model — the problem, the code, the change, and how to
know it worked. It is `gx review`'s own fix plan narrowed to one item, so the two
never disagree. Pipes cleanly: `gx enhance | claude -p "apply this"`.

**Reviews survive the terminal** — Every run that inspected code saves its full JSON
report to `review/review-findings-<timestamp>.json`, git-excluded automatically.
`--md` prints the PR-comment shape, and `--fast` trades the second reviewer and the
verification pass for wall clock when someone is waiting.

## July 29, 2026

**PR summary verdict labels** — The summary's triage line now states what the reader
must do, not just a color: 🟢 **Quick scan** (LOW), 🟡 **Careful pass** (MEDIUM),
🔴 **Deep review** (HIGH). The label is enforced server-side to always match the
Blast Radius level, so a red summary can never read as permission to skim.

**A new name** — The product is now **gx**. The CLI is `gx` (`gxr` for one-shot review,
`gx-mcp` for agents). Install from `download.gx.run`; docs live at
[gx.run/docs](/docs).

## July 26, 2026

**Plain Git is the whole workflow** — Capture and publishing are entirely hook-driven:
`git commit` records a revision, `git push` captures the session and publishes. The
porcelain that duplicated Git (`gx push`, `gx sync`, the background daemon, and the
macOS menu-bar app) has been removed. If you have an older install, `gx init` cleans
up the retired pieces.

**PR summaries write to the description** — gx Cloud writes the rich summary
into the pull request description below your own text, behind a gx-owned
marker. Your notes survive every regeneration.

**`gx review` is guaranteed read-only** — Review writes nothing: no repo state, no
`.git/index` mutation, no `~/.gx` on machines that never ran `gx`, and no
uploads when a gate fails. `--fail-on` turns a review into a CI gate with distinct
exit codes for "findings survived" and "nothing was reviewed". See the
[CLI reference](/docs/cli#gx-review).

*Updated [August 16, 2026](#august-16-2026): review now saves its JSON report to
`review/` (git-excluded, the one file it writes), gates on blocking findings by
default, and exits 5 when the panel ran degraded.*

**Two-model review panel** — `gx review` runs two independent Anthropic reviewers
plus a judge that verifies and dedupes findings. When both reviewers flag the same
issue independently, the report says so — the strongest confidence signal a panel
produces.

## July 2, 2026

**Generated GitHub PR summaries** — After you publish with plain `git push` and open
a PR, gx Cloud posts a generated review summary highlighting blast radius and
high-impact review targets.

**Code review history memory** — `gx review` pulls in indexed context from your past
reviews and GitHub comment history, and attaches review policy context so findings
stay consistent with how your team reviews code.

**Prompted `gx review`** — Trigger `gx review` with a targeted prompt to focus the
review on a specific concern instead of the full default sweep.

*Updated [August 16, 2026](#august-16-2026): the positional argument is an intent, not
a focusing prompt — use `--scope` and `--focus` to narrow a review.*
